questions.q: In the Northbridge pipeline, what triggers an automatic deploy to the staging namespace?
options: Any commit to any branch
Pushing a semver git tag, such as v1.4.0
Opening a pull request
Manually running a script on a laptop
questions.explain: A semver tag push auto-deploys to the staging namespace; production requires an additional manual approval gate beyond that.

questions.q: How does GitHub Actions authenticate to Azure in the Northbridge pipeline without storing long-lived credentials?
options: A service principal secret stored as a GitHub repository secret
OIDC federation, where Azure AD trusts a short-lived token issued per workflow run
A shared admin password rotated annually
SSH keys checked into the repository
questions.explain: OIDC federated credentials let Azure AD trust short-lived, scoped tokens GitHub issues per run, eliminating the need to store any long-lived cloud secret.

questions.q: What is the key difference between blue-green and canary deployments?
options: They are the same strategy with different names
Blue-green cuts all traffic over at once between two environments; canary shifts a small percentage of traffic first and ramps up gradually
Canary deployments require no monitoring
Blue-green only works for stateless services
questions.explain: Blue-green is an all-or-nothing cutover between two full environments, while canary gradually increases traffic to the new version while watching metrics.

questions.q: Where do application secrets like the PaymentPro API key live in the Northbridge architecture, and how do they reach running pods?
options: Hardcoded in the Helm values files committed to git
In Azure Key Vault, synced into Kubernetes Secrets at runtime by the External Secrets Operator
Pasted into GitHub Actions workflow YAML
Emailed between team members
questions.explain: Key Vault holds the real secret values, and the External Secrets Operator syncs them into Kubernetes Secrets, so nothing sensitive is ever committed to git or CI.

questions.q: Why would canary deployment paired with Prometheus/Grafana be a good fit specifically for the checkout service?
options: Checkout has no SLO, so monitoring doesn't matter
Checkout has an explicit latency SLO, and canary with live metrics can catch a regression before it reaches all flash-sale traffic
Canary deployments eliminate the need for any testing
Product-catalog requires canary, not checkout
questions.explain: Checkout's 99.5% under-800ms-p99 SLO means catching a regression early, on a small slice of traffic, has real value — exactly what canary plus live dashboards enables.
